Params: Approaching the designated altitude, Commander Adelyde. Any lower and we'll reach the Comet Patrol Array's alert perimeter.
All units, hold position. Deploy drones to scout ahead. We need to confirm whether the Comet system is still operational.
The crew holds their breath as a reconnaissance drone with its own ID code descends. The moment it crosses an invisible threshold, it explodes in a flash.
The laser leaves nothing behind, not even debris.

In the distance, a Comet unit retracts its cannon and falls back into formation. The engineers in the cabin look devastated: their prized defense system is proving itself devastatingly effective at the worst possible time.
Report: half the drones dispatched have been destroyed, but the other half made it through!
Is there any pattern to how the array is identifying friend from foe?
We're looking into it, but without knowing how badly the Atlantic Eye's central system is damaged, we're missing too many variables to run the numbers.
The transport craft can be docked mid-air... Could we use the ones that already passed through to ferry the remaining personnel and equipment down?
But the family's ID code is dynamic! How can we be sure that Comet will still register us as friendlies next time?
What about the IFF code between the Comet units?
Every eye in the room turns to you.
They're still coordinating. I haven't seen them attack each other.
The IFF code between Comet units runs on a completely separate system. From the looks of it, at least that part is still intact...
Could we then capture a Comet unit and have it fly with us, so that it interferes with the array's IFF identification?
The family engineer turns to Adelyde with a stumbling look, his expression caught somewhere between awe and sheer terror.
Commander, are you seriously planning to take a transport craft and go toe-to-toe with Comet?
I won't put any of you at risk, so we'll split up. I'll take down a Comet unit while you get the towing gear ready to catch it.
Contact the carrier below and ask them to prepare a Silverwing-9 for me. I'll be boarding shortly.
Make that two. I'm coming with you.
You've never dealt with a Comet unit before. This is a very dangerous last resort.
But everyone will be in danger if we don't deal with it soon.
Have you forgotten how expertly I manned the flight stabilizer back then?
We've got a situation! A Comet unit is heading straight for us!
Shields up! Deploy energy shields now! Prepare the weapons!
Adelyde grabs the onboard telescope and swings it toward the Comet unit.
Someone's piloting the unit manually. No autopilot flies this terribly.
The subject of her remark is currently spiraling through the air erratically, accompanied by a distorted shriek crackling over its speaker.
Don't tell me that's from the speaker installed for the Day of Enlightenment celebration... Who puts a megaphone on a fighter jet...?
Left, left, left... no, too far! Who the hell calibrated this flight stick—
Hey, you good people over there! You're here to save us, right?
We are. Can you report on the situation inside the Atlantic Eye, and tell us how to get in?
The situation is hard to explain quickly, so just assume the worst... Honestly, I can't bring myself to think about it too hard either, or I won't be able to function.

Anyway, the Comet unit we're in can bring you down, and I'm sending you the coordinates of a docking port that's still intact. Once you're inside, stay away from any dangerous-looking energy, then follow the golden threads.
Wait, how do you know about that?
Those golden threads are the only reason I'm still alive to talk to you right now. Follow them, and you'll find a survivor camp at the very least. That's where you'll find me.
The chatty Comet unit wobbles out of sight. Then, you hear a loud clunk from somewhere beneath the hull of your transport craft.
Uh, the camera is showing that it's latched onto the underside of our cabin like a starfish.
The distant voice cuts out for a moment, barely audible over the engine noise.
P-please... please hurry and find me. I'm begging you.
We will. Please, don't give up.
Crew, keep the energy shield up just in case. We'll move in toward the alert perimeter.
The engines roar as the ship descends toward the dam below.
It worked! The other Comet units aren't attacking us!
Orders flow down the chain of command with practiced ease. As that happens, Adelyde pulls you into a corner of the cabin, hoping to talk to her "informant and confidant."
I didn't have time to ask earlier, but... the fact that you're appearing here in the flesh at this point in time... Does that mean what you're looking for is here?
Ananke is why I'm here, and it's the key for me to go back.
A complicated expression crosses Adelyde's face. She turns away and draws a long, slow breath, as though the words she is about to say are ones she cannot bear to repeat.
When we're down there, the moment you believe the time is right, the moment you can go back... you go.
I will. There's a whole future of people waiting for me.
But before that, we'll look into the truth behind this disaster and Ananke.
Your future is my past. We only have this one world between us.
Don't even think I'd leave you behind.
Adelyde takes your hand and clutches it, giving you her answer without a word.
The fear and reluctance buried deep in her red eyes quietly dissolve under your gaze. What remains is nothing but calm.
She still remembers stepping down the gangway amid the roar of the propellers, her feet touching the dam for the very first time.

The docking port sat a hundred meters above the sea, waves crashing against its base structure far below. Pushed by instinctive fear and pulled by a tingling rush of excitement, she ran toward the edge of the dam.
Night sank its harp to the ocean floor, and dawn plucked the strings with a blush of rose-colored light.
Ships moaned like whales as they cut through white-crested waves. The beacon tower blazed without rest, its light calling sea and sky alike to fix their gaze upon it.
Her young heart brimmed with vitality, and Rusalka laughed softly behind her, telling her to hurry up and keep moving.
The load-bearing structures below are too damaged. We can't set up camp here!
Fall back. Our priority is to set up a comms relay to stay in contact with the global reinforcement. Can we still get a signal from the beacon tower?
No good. It's gone completely dark.
Hauling a heavy portable generator, she retreats to the back of the group, nearly tripping on something. She looks down to find a collapsed sign reading "Port A054".
Behind her, the megastructure lets out a groan as its arms shear away, sending walls of murky waves crashing up from below.
<size=60>She has nothing to look back to.</size>
She still remembers slipping away from a banquet where she had nothing to say and no desire to speak. Back then, she hid in the memorial garden nestled in the underwater city directly above the hall.
The city built for the future reserved a small corner of its heart for history. Upon moonstone tiles, mercury and gold traced the long journey humanity had traveled.
From diving underwater with a hollow reed clenched between the teeth, and crossing rivers in hollowed-out logs...

To venturing to the deepest trenches of the ocean, communing with traces from eons past. At depths where pressure crushed, extinct flora bloomed once more, and miniature wonders carved from crystal were kept preserved.
Footsteps shattered the silence. She spun around, instantly on guard.
Are you... Miss Helio? The one my father mentioned he'd introduce me to?
Huh? You're hiding out here too?
Pleasure to meet you, our fellow rascal!
Before she could react, the two girls grabbed her hand and shook it, leading her deeper down the path.
The submersible boat bursts out of an as-yet-unflooded emergency tunnel, plunging into a world gone wrong.
Bridges and elevated rails hang frozen mid-air, suspended in the moment of their collapse, while the enormous towers are melting like iron in a furnace.
The trail she ran on each morning.
The training grounds where she pushed herself through afternoon drills.
The garden where she wandered at dusk.
The hangar bay that hummed with quiet order late at night.
All of it is gone. Every trace of the life she lived has dissolved into a surge of luminous blue.
In a world torn violently apart, the rescue team begins to encounter what used to be people.
A pinned figure is struggling beneath the rubble. Half of him is still flesh and blood, but the other half is slowly dissipating into drifting motes of blue light.
The rescue team member snaps a vital signs monitor onto the survivor's wrist. Adelyde kneels over him, carefully cradling the back of his neck.
I want to go home... Mama... Ma...
I've got an ID on him! Professor Hell, Director of the Third Laboratory at the Current Power Output Center—
The fear, the pain, and the pleading in his eyes are all gone within seconds, leaving nothing but a pure void.
W-why... does he sound like an infant...?
It's not just his voice. His entire consciousness regressed just now.
Her hands suddenly feel lighter. As if carried off by wind, the luminous ash slips away between her fingers.
The vital signs monitor clatters to the ground, and only an empty lab coat remains beneath the rubble.
What are we even doing here?! This is a graveyard! All... all of it was just an illusion—
An energy arc explodes out of the rubbles without warning, grazing past the team member's nose as Adelyde wrenches him back by force.
He crumples to the ground, unable to move.
Adelyde grabs him by the collar and hauls him up.
I wish this were all just an illusion, but it's not.
The places and people the explosion took from us are gone, but we're still here. And the people who sent those Comet units to bring us here are still waiting for us.
You have one minute to pull yourself together. If you can't, get in an escape pod and go back. Don't throw your life away.
She raises her terminal without another glance at him.
All units, report your status on the search for the golden threads.
Amid the static, the noise, and the ragged breathing, the chime of a successful connection has never sounded so sweet.
This is Unit 007! We've found the golden threads!
The unit closest to the marked route besides Unit 007 is us, Commander.
The conditions here are too unstable. All units, move at your own pace. Don't wait for each other.
In the vast, silent chaos, the faint light guiding your team forward flickers like the lure of a deep-sea fish.
Depth scanner's showing that we're close to the bottom of the city.
The markings at the edge of your vision flicker. The streams of light that once held you steady through the Consciousness Tide gather around you, drawing close point by point.
I came searching for Ananke, and it seems to be searching for me too.
That thought strikes you like lightning, and you whisper that to Adelyde.
As the team presses on and follows the golden threads, she gives your arm a quiet squeeze to encourage you to share your memory.
And maybe, just maybe, it can pass messages between different spacetime coordinates through whatever network the rays form. A pipeline system, an ant colony's tunnels, superhighways—take your pick.
If that's true, and the energy is from the Consciousness Tide...
Could the information flowing through Ananke actually be human consciousness?
Commander! The golden threads are pointing to that intact building!
The blast door swings open, and a pink-haired figure in an engineer's uniform stands in the doorway.
He waves frantically toward the rescue team. Then, slowly, his body begins to shake as he crumples to his knees with his hands pressed over his face.
Amidst the devastation, this stretch of building stands like a piece of amber, held together by a web of golden threads and untouched by the glowing blue tide.
The lights are still on. A doormat lies kicked askew, and a row of half-neglected plants sits along the windowsill.

It is as if the structure is stuck at the ordinary morning before the explosion, when people would grumble about the free coffee, clock in right on the hour, and absently water the potted plants on their way in.
Adelyde breaks into a sprint, rushing toward Aristo at incredible speed.
Are you hurt? How are you holding up? What are you doing here?
I-I'm fine, my legs just... gave out a little. I was the one who brought you down here.
Yeah. I never got the chance to tell you that I made it onto the Comet project. Full-time.
His face drained of color, he pushes himself up off the ground.

Behind the door on the left is where we've been keeping the survivors. My colleagues who know first aid are looking after them. Anyone who can be moved needs to be moved now, because this place won't hold much longer.
When the disaster first struck, there were 4 floors preserved in the building behind us. After less than 16 hours, there are only 2 left.
No, send your team. You come with me. I have a way to reach the other survivor camps.
And bring the person on your team who knows about Ananke.
Aristo gives a quick nod, flicks his lab coat back, and takes off toward the lower floor. You and Adelyde immediately follow him.
The most devastating thing after the explosion was the sudden collapse of our control system. If a giant is stripped of its nervous system, it is nothing but dead weight.
But then, out of nowhere, a system with no prior development record called Ananke came online.
Everyone jumped on reverse-engineering it right away. What we discovered was that beyond keeping this place standing, its most critical function was—
He slams the security lock on the door to the lower floor. It bursts open, and an array of massive quantum computer screens fills your view.

Pale golden streams of data weave into a dense lattice against the black display like nerves and roots, propping up the collapsed control systems. A few focused figures hunch over their terminals, paying you no mind.
To the side, a strange device shaped like an hourglass is pulsing streams of light. They are linking the quantum computers together, but they are also projected into the distance through the walls.
That hourglass is Ananke's sub-unit. It connects the quantum terminals at each location into Ananke's Link, and every point we can reach is a survivor camp.
71 in total, but that number might shrink. Ananke's output is decreasing.
What about the areas you can't reach?
Aristo turns away. He tries to speak, but no words come out.
In this miraculous megastructure that spans thousands of square miles, only 71 crumbling pockets are left.
The pinnacle of oceanic exploration throughout all of human history, the sum of the TEC's wisdom and toil, the most beautiful mark humanity could ever leave upon this earth—
Its future ended the moment the disaster struck.
A crushing grief floods the room, as those who built a civilization are now burying it. You wish you did not understand what that feels like.
But if this bitter road has taught you anything at all, it is that disasters do not pity people's grief. People simply endure.
You said Ananke won't last, but I know it was built to cover the whole dam.
But if it can keep running at current capacity, we can rescue the 71 camps.

Ananke's Link does have access points in it, and the biggest one is likely the master node, which differs from the distribution nodes. We confirmed its existence, but it's too deep in. We didn't have the resources to reach it.
He walks over to the control panel in front of the screens and reaches out to one of his colleagues there, pulling back the sleeve of that person's lab coat.
There is no flesh beneath it, just a shimmer of blue, glowing dust in the shape of a person.
You must have seen what those energy surges do to people on your way here. They didn't have time to get clear, only make their way inside after they were hit.
The dissolution of their consciousnesses happens slowly, bit by bit.

Forgetting the hypothesis they proved at 50, the critical breakthrough they achieved late at night at 40, the title of their doctoral thesis at 30, the times they had to grind through even the easiest experiment at 20...

The warmth of family and friends, the excitement that makes you want to sing, the relief of bringing something to fruition after days without rest, the pride of getting it right after countless failures.
Whether a life was brilliant or not, it must be something precious to the one who lived it... something that couldn't be willingly let go of.
So when every other means of saving themselves had failed, they used neural interfaces to plug themselves into Ananke's Link.
Only now do you and Adelyde look closely at the data streaming across the large screen.

"Topology Reconstruction of Transoceanic Backbone Networks Under Strong Whirlpool Interference". "Seismic Applications of Lunar Rock Composite Materials". "Long-Term Effects of Flow Diversion Systems on North Atlantic Thermohaline Circulation"...
Papers, monographs, lab records, blueprints, calculations, technical tutorials...
From the Atlantic Eye's first conception to its final completion, every trace of effort left behind by generations of scientists, engineers, maritime workers, and sailors is here.
They've uploaded their knowledge into Ananke?
More than that. They're also exporting research secrets that were stored exclusively within the Atlantic Eye.
He smiles wryly at the row of memory chips slotted in along the terminals.
Adelyde, tell me... Once the family gets their hands on all of this, do you think they'll build a second Atlantic Eye?
A flicker of conflict crosses Adelyde's red eyes. Her nails dig into her palm, but her voice comes out soft.
While we are out here risking our lives, the Great Family Council is probably just voting on damage reports and cutting their losses.
The Atlantic Eye's work will be carved up and folded into new projects. Its name will be erased and treated as a stain.
You're still as blunt as ever...
But the spirit of the Atlantic Eye will never die.
There is such certainty in her voice that, for a fleeting moment, you glimpse the crimson figure she will one day become.
Whatever the world may say of them in the years to come, the people of the Atlantic Eye started with good intentions, and they held on until the very end.
It wasn't just the great dam that was gazing at the stars from the ocean floor. We were too.
Send the rescue teams to the sub-units to get the people out. Gray Raven and I will find the main control room of Ananke.
We won't let the Atlantic Eye close its eyes like this.
The boy who was once startled by a grenade closes his eyes; the finest engineer the TEC will ever produce lifts his head.
Leave me a deep-dive suit. I'll stay until the export is complete.
Don't worry. I value my skin too much to die here, so I'll crawl out if I have to.
He presses a terminal into Adelyde's hands. Ananke's Link is blinking on its screen.
Take care of yourself, Captain Adelyde. See you up there.
<size=50>How does one describe a disaster from inside it? How does one fish tears out of the ocean?</size>
The lone white-haired figure pulls you aboard the fastest submersible boat and dives into the dark and the vast unknown.
You hold the terminal connected to Ananke's Link in your hands. Desperate, frantic, chaotic voices flood in from every corner of this ocean, echoing through both your earpieces.
This is Unit 034. A surge hit our boat, and our whole crew is gone. Awaiting extraction. We... we did our best.
This is submarine cable and data hub server room 41. Export is complete, but the rescue team hasn't arrived yet. We've placed the chips on the Ananke sub-units, so please... at least get them out.
This is Spelmin Family Squad 8. We've picked up the survivors rescued by Units 021 and 025, and we're heading to the last coordinates transmitted by Unit 011. Unit 011, do you copy?
This is Aeris of the F.O.S. medical team. Does anyone in the area have atropine injectors to spare?
We can't reach the target depth. Our hull damage is causing an energy leak—
Adelyde wrenches the rudder hard to evade a surge. The luminous blue light grows blinding, and she is sailing almost entirely on instinct now.
Every call for help is a place you cannot reach in time.
Want me to take your earpiece off?
Focus on sailing. I'll handle the transmissions.
The blue light is reflected in her eyes like the blue heart of a flame.
More voices join the comms: quiet ones, wistful ones, desperate ones.

Good thing Tavis isn't here today. Our project's gone, so I guess he can overlook the times I screwed up... Though, I always knew he was a softie inside, even with his own daughters. He taught me a lot... Thank you.

Before I fully forget myself, I'm leaving one last request: is there any unit that can free my Huhu along the way? They can survive on their own in the ocean. They're not defective... They're my babies.
This is Murphy from Current Ecology Station One. Listen up, Jules Romeu... I didn't marry you for that big brain of yours. I married you because I love you.
Whoever receives this, please visit the home of Ethan from Turbine Maintenance Team Three... And if you can, be a better family member than he was.

A flood of blue and gold swirls around you, and up and down is indistinguishable from each other. Your boat is seemingly drifting through a nebula, witnessing every joy and sorrow of humanity at a place farthest from it.
Amid the blare of the low-power alarm, the markings at the edge of your vision grow brighter.
The central control room that should theoretically exist is still nowhere in sight.
Then, a familiar voice flows through from the terminal in your hand, clear and cool as a spring.
This is Arakna, F.O.S. Support Team One. Adelyde, are you there?
The boat stops. Adelyde slowly leans forward in her seat, her hair covering her face.
I sent my students ahead with the survivors and the chips. I couldn't reach Helentine either.
The surge took my right leg. I don't have much time left before the Ananke node here dies, and there's something I need to say before it's too late.
When you came looking for me at Port A054 that year... I was there. I watched you from a distance.
I couldn't bring myself to see you, because I realized that I still wanted to believe in you, despite hating everything that made you who you are.
I could never make peace with my life. In an age everyone else celebrates, my future always feels like a canvas torn away before the painting is even half-finished.
I don't regret being the one who ruined the scene, or standing alongside those who never felt like they belonged. But I still don't know if I should regret not going to see you that day.
Adelyde's shoulders pull taut. Her words are fraying at the edges, and her fingers are pressing into the metal dashboard so hard that they almost leave a mark.
Don't let me hold you back.
Dreaming of sailing the stars, standing up against tyranny, throwing herself into the fire for her belief... my friend has never once looked back.
A long, quiet sigh comes through from the other end of the terminal.
Be a little kinder to yourself, Adelyde. Stop putting everyone else first. Just tell me...
All those years you kept your distance from me... Did you miss me?
If nothing else, I owe you an apology for that.
I don't have much to leave you. I know the price of standing against your family, so if you ever find yourself with nowhere to go, I've left you a letter of recommendation to teach at F.O.S.
The Day of Enlightenment is almost here. It's been many years since we last celebrated, but I haven't forgotten the tradition.
I'm giving you my wish, Adelyde.
Go find your joy and freedom, on the other side of the pain.
Ananke's Link goes dark on the terminal.
One drop, two drops, three... Tears fall from her face silently, and she sobs like a small animal in pain.
No longer able to hold it back, Adelyde breaks down.
(Put an arm around her shoulders and give a gentle squeeze)
We don't know where Ananke can lead. It's worth a shot.
Adelyde lifts her tear-streaked face and looks up.
We only have enough power to enter the Ananke rays.
We've given everything we have. The rest is up to fate.
I do not walk alone, and I will never give up.
The boat sails forward at full speed and plunges into a sea of golden light.
